question: Which CAPEC patterns map to ATT&CK technique T1133 (External Remote Services), and what is that technique?

answer.headline: Gathered 2 record(s) from 2 source(s); 1 cross-source correlation(s) on shared identifiers.
answer.narrative: The CAPEC pattern Remote Services with Stolen Credentials (CAPEC-555) maps to the ATT&CK technique T1133. T1133, known as External Remote Services, is a technique where adversaries leverage external-facing remote services such as VPNs or Citrix to initially access or persist within a network.

records.name: Remote Services with Stolen Credentials
records.label: AttackPattern
records.description: This pattern of attack involves an adversary that uses stolen credentials to leverage remote services such as RDP, telnet, SSH, and VNC to log into a system. Once access is gained, any number of malicious activities could be performed.

results.query: MATCH (n:Technique) WHERE n.attack_id IN $ids OPTIONAL MATCH (n)-[r]-(m) WITH n, CASE WHEN m IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE type(r) END AS rel, CASE WHEN m IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE startNode(r) = n END AS outgoing, CASE WHEN m IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE head(labels(m)) END AS neighbour_label, count(m) AS cnt WITH n, collect(CASE WHEN rel IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE {rel: rel, outgoing: outgoing, label: neighbour_label, count: cnt} END) AS raw WITH n, [f IN raw WHERE f IS NOT NULL] AS facets RETURN n.attack_id AS id, n.name AS name, n.properties_json AS properties_json, facets AS facets LIMIT 300

records.name: External Remote Services
records.label: Technique
records.description: Adversaries may leverage external-facing remote services to initially access and/or persist within a network. Remote services such as VPNs, Citrix, and other access mechanisms allow users to connect to internal enterprise network resources from external locations. There are often remote service gateways that manage connections and credential authentication for these services.
